title: DEFLECT: Temporal Counterfactual Preference Learning for Delay-Robust Asynchronous VLAs
abstract: arXiv:2605.19294v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies increasingly rely on asynchronous inference to hide model latency behind ongoing robot motion. During inference, the robot continues executing its current action chunk while the next chunk is generated from the observation available at inference start. By the time the new chunk is executed, the robot or scene may have changed, so an action that fits the prediction-time state can be misaligned with the execution-time state. Training-time methods modify the policy input or supervised target based on the expected execution delay, but do not directly supervise how actions should change as the scene evolves between prediction and execution. Runtime repair methods improve chunk continuity or modify actions during deployment, but can still leave actions aligned with the prediction-time state rather than the execution-time state. translated_title: DEFLECT：面向延迟鲁棒异步视觉-语言-动作模型的时序反事实偏好学习
translated_abstract: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略越来越依赖于异步推理，将模型延迟隐藏在机器人持续运动之中。在推理期间，机器人继续执行当前的动作块，同时基于推理开始时可获得的观测生成下一个动作块。等到新动作块被执行时，机器人或场景可能已经发生变化，因此适合预测时刻状态的动作可能与执行时刻的状态不一致。训练时方法基于预期的执行延迟修改策略输入或监督目标，但并未直接监督动作应如何随场景在预测与执行之间的演变而变化。运行时修复方法改善了动作块的连续性或在部署期间修改动作，但仍可能使动作与预测时刻状态而非执行时刻状态保持一致。我们的关键洞察是，执行时刻的观测是不可用的（摘要内容在此处被截断）。
tldr: 提出DEFLECT框架，通过时序反事实偏好学习直接监督动作应如何随预测与执行之间的场景演变而调整，从而提升异步VLA策略对推理延迟的鲁棒性。
en_tdlr: DEFLECT introduces temporal counterfactual preference learning to directly supervise how actions should adapt as scenes evolve between prediction and execution, making asynchronous VLA policies robust to inference delays.
